indication: newly-diagnosed advanced high-grade serous/endometrioid ovarian cancer
inclusion_match_notes: SOLO1 enrolls the patient's tumor type, stage, and 1L-maintenance setting after platinum response, which she matches. It restricts maintenance to BRCA-mutated tumors; her germline BRCA is wild-type and somatic BRCA is still pending, so eligibility hinges on the unresulted tumor NGS. Fit is partial until that gating assay returns.
intervention_dosing: olaparib 300 mg PO BID, up to 2 years

indication: newly-diagnosed advanced ovarian cancer at high risk of recurrence
inclusion_match_notes: PRIMA matches her indication, stage, and 1L-maintenance timing and gives a benefit in all-comers regardless of BRCA or HRD status, so unlike SOLO1 it does not strictly require the pending tumor assay. The magnitude is larger in the HRD-positive subgroup (HR 0.43), so the pending genomic-instability score still refines expected benefit. Thrombocytopenia and other cytopenias are common and bump against her myelosuppression veto.
intervention_dosing: niraparib 200-300 mg PO once daily (individualized starting dose), up to 3 years

indication: newly-diagnosed advanced high-grade serous/endometrioid ovarian cancer
design: double-blind randomized placebo-controlled, all on bevacizumab (PAOLA-1)
inclusion_match_notes: PAOLA-1 is the closest design match: every patient receives bevacizumab maintenance, which she is already on, and olaparib is added on top. The PFS benefit concentrates in HRD-positive tumors (HR 0.33 with BRCA, 0.43 without), so her pending HRD/genomic-instability score gates whether the olaparib add-on is worthwhile. Adding a PARP inhibitor to ongoing bevacizumab also compounds bleeding/VTE caution given her high-VTE history and prior IVC filter.
intervention_dosing: olaparib 300 mg PO BID + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV q3w; olaparib up to 2 years, bevacizumab 15 months total

indication: newly-diagnosed advanced epithelial ovarian cancer (stage III-IV)
inclusion_match_notes: ATHENA-MONO tests rucaparib 1L maintenance in her exact stage III-IV first-line setting and stratifies by HRD, with a stronger ITT benefit than placebo. Her germline-BRCA-wild-type status leaves HRD-subgroup placement dependent on the pending tumor assay, holding fit at partial. Anemia and other cytopenias are the dominant toxicity and engage her myelosuppression veto.
intervention_dosing: rucaparib 600 mg PO BID, up to 2 years

indication: newly-diagnosed advanced epithelial ovarian / fallopian-tube / primary-peritoneal cancer
inclusion_match_notes: GOG-218 establishes the bevacizumab maintenance regimen she is already receiving in her exact indication, stage, and 1L setting, so it is the direct evidence base for continuing her current anti-angiogenic axis. The PFS gain came only from the bevacizumab-throughout (maintenance) arm, matching her trajectory. Her high-VTE history and prior IVC filter warrant ongoing bleeding/thrombosis monitoring on bevacizumab, though that risk is already accepted in her current plan.
intervention_dosing: bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV q3w with chemo then maintenance to ~15 months

indication: newly-diagnosed ovarian cancer (incl. high-risk stage IIIc/IV)
inclusion_match_notes: ICON7 supports bevacizumab maintenance in her 1L setting and showed the largest benefit in the high-risk subgroup (stage IIIc with residual disease or stage IV), which overlaps her presentation prior to R0 resection. It reinforces the anti-angiogenic axis she is already on. Bleeding and thrombotic events are the relevant cautions given her VTE history.
intervention_dosing: bevacizumab 7.5 mg/kg IV q3w with chemo then maintenance to 12 months

inclusion_match_notes: NRG-GY004 pairs the PARP (HRD) and anti-angiogenic (VEGFR via cediranib) axes she carries, but in the recurrent platinum-sensitive line rather than her 1L-maintenance setting, so it informs a later-line combination rather than her current decision. The oral olaparib-cediranib combination did not beat chemotherapy on PFS overall. It anchors the chemo-free oral doublet option for if and when she recurs.
intervention_dosing: olaparib 200 mg PO BID + cediranib 30 mg PO once daily

design: prospective cohort with matched control validation
inclusion_match_notes: This cohort targets exactly her ER-positive high-grade serous biology and tests letrozole as low-burden oral maintenance, which fits her age, tolerability priorities, and stated preference for oral therapy. The signal is real but non-randomized, so the evidence tier is weaker than the PARP and bevacizumab RCTs. Her PR-negativity tempers the expected magnitude of endocrine benefit.

indication: ER/PR-positive recurrent/metastatic granulosa-cell / sex-cord stromal ovarian tumours
inclusion_match_notes: PARAGON tests the same endocrine mechanism (aromatase inhibition for ER-positive ovarian disease) the patient could use, but in granulosa-cell/sex-cord stromal tumours rather than her high-grade serous histology, so it is mechanism-precedent rather than an enrolling match. It is included to show the aromatase-inhibitor clinical-benefit signal in ER-positive ovarian disease. The high stable-disease rate supports endocrine therapy as a low-toxicity holding option, not a strong cytoreductive one.

indication: newly-diagnosed advanced ovarian / fallopian-tube / primary-peritoneal cancer
design: phase I/II IMNN-001 + bevacizumab + neoadjuvant chemotherapy with second-look
inclusion_match_notes: This trial mirrors the patient's own on-study regimen of IL-12 immunogene therapy plus bevacizumab on a neoadjuvant carboplatin/paclitaxel backbone in newly-diagnosed advanced disease, so it is her direct on-study context rather than a new option. It anchors the board's reasoning about the IL-12/tumor-microenvironment axis she is already receiving. Toxicity has been manageable with the intraperitoneal immunogene approach in prior GEN-1 studies.
intervention_dosing: GEN-1 (IMNN-001) intraperitoneal weekly + bevacizumab IV + carboplatin/paclitaxel

indication: newly-diagnosed FIGO stage III/IV ovarian cancer (neoadjuvant)
design: randomized phase I/II IMNN-001 (GEN-1) + NACT vs NACT (OVATION 2)
inclusion_match_notes: OVATION 2 is the randomized IL-12 immunogene study underpinning the patient's on-study GEN-1/IMNN-001 program, in the same neoadjuvant stage III/IV setting she was treated in. It provides the efficacy and safety context for the IL-12 axis the board needs. The IMNN-001 arm reported encouraging PFS and surgical-response signals that motivated the phase 3.
intervention_dosing: GEN-1 (IMNN-001) 79-100 mg/m2 intraperitoneal weekly + neoadjuvant carboplatin/paclitaxel

design: randomized phase 3 IMNN-001 + standard NACT/adjuvant chemo +/- PARP maintenance (OVATION 3)
intervention: GEN-1 (IMNN-001) + carboplatin/paclitaxel +/- olaparib or niraparib maintenance
inclusion_match_notes: This phase 3 advances the patient's IL-12 immunogene axis into the registrational setting and explicitly allows PARP-inhibitor maintenance alongside IMNN-001, so it links two of her targetable features in one protocol. It enrolls her exact newly-diagnosed advanced ovarian indication. Whether a PARP arm applies to her still depends on the pending HRD/somatic-BRCA result.
intervention_dosing: GEN-1 (IMNN-001) intraperitoneal + carboplatin/paclitaxel; optional olaparib/niraparib maintenance per HRD
